homepage_url_justification: The pkgdown homepage is https://pagerankr-63ad30.gitlab.io/ and is the first URL in DESCRIPTION's URL field: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
sites_https_justification: The project homepage, source repository, and development distribution are all served over HTTPS: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr , https://pagerankr-63ad30.gitlab.io/ , and https://bart-turczynski.r-universe.dev/pagerankr .
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and the project homepage succinctly describe pagerankr as an R toolkit for PageRank modelling on crawl and analytics data: https://pagerankr-63ad30.gitlab.io/
interact_justification: The project homepage links to installation, documentation, bug reporting, and contribution information; contribution instructions are at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue tracker is https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents acceptable contribution requirements: tests, lintr, R CMD check, and the local pre-push and GitLab CI verification gates: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE is at the repository top level: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: Basic documentation covers installation, getting started, usage (with a tutorial-style vignette), and secure use. Install/quick-start instructions and worked examples are in the README and on the pkgdown site: https://pagerankr-63ad30.gitlab.io/ ; the usage tutorial vignette is at https://pagerankr-63ad30.gitlab.io/articles/pagerankr-usage.html ; guidance on safely handling untrusted crawl/URL/link-graph input is in SECURITY.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function has roxygen2-generated reference documentation describing arguments and return values: https://pagerankr-63ad30.gitlab.io/reference/index.html
repo_public_justification: Source is publicly available at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr (GitHub carries a read-only mirror).
repo_track_justification: All source changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are publicly available between releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique DESCRIPTION Version (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/DESCRIPTION) with a matching NEWS.md heading (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md); the first release, 0.1.0, is recorded with its source commit in CRAN-SUBMISSION: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/CRAN-SUBMISSION
version_semver_justification: The package uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning, visible in DESCRIPTION and NEWS.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
version_tags_justification: Not yet: the repository has no release tags. 0.1.0 was submitted to CRAN from a recorded commit (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/CRAN-SUBMISSION) but was not tagged. CI is ready for v* tags (check-oldrel runs on them: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml), so tagging releases would meet this.
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md documents user-facing changes for each release: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records all changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab work items (issues) are the public issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports through the GitLab issue tracker, as the README's Contributing section directs: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
report_responses_justification: The maintainer acknowledges and responds to bug reports in the public tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are accepted and responded to through the GitLab issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
report_archive_justification: The GitLab issue tracker is a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in SECURITY.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md (also rendered at https://pagerankr-63ad30.gitlab.io/SECURITY.html )
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md names private email to the maintainer as the preferred channel, with a GitLab confidential issue (visible only to project members) as the alternative: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within seven days and coordinating a fix and disclosure: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: The package builds with the standard R toolchain and R CMD check; the reproducible CI configuration is GitLab CI: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
build_common_tools_justification: It uses standard R build tooling and GitLab CI: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
build_floss_tools_justification: R and its build toolchain are free/open-source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_justification: The FLOSS testthat suite is public and its invocation is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and CI: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
test_invocation_justification: Tests use the standard testthat invocation (devtools::test() or testthat::test_local()) and run as part of R CMD check, which CONTRIBUTING.md documents as a step of the pre-push gate: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: Coverage is measured with covr by the coverage job in https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml and reported through GitLab's own coverage reporting (the README coverage badge); no third-party service is involved.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires testing and verification of changes before push: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major functionality is accompanied by focused testthat files in the public suite: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
tests_documented_added_justification: The contribution and verification expectations are documented in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: Warnings are surfaced via R CMD check and lintr in the GitLab CI gates and check jobs (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml) and in the pre-push hook (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.githooks/pre-push).
warnings_fixed_justification: The pre-push gate fails on R CMD check warnings and errors, and the CI check job sets error_on = "warning": https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.githooks/pre-push
warnings_strict_justification: The CI gates job sets LINTR_ERROR_ON_LINT=true so any lint fails the build (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml), and the pre-push R CMD check runs --as-cran and fails on warnings (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.githooks/pre-push).
know_secure_design_justification: The package defensively processes untrusted URL, redirect, crawl, and link-graph data.
know_common_errors_justification: Input validation and tests cover malformed inputs, redirect loops, and graph edge cases.
crypto_password_storage_justification: pagerankr stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: pagerankr does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_used_network_justification: pagerankr does not itself make network connections.
crypto_tls12_justification: pagerankr does not establish network connections.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: pagerankr does not establish network connections.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: pagerankr does not establish network connections.
delivery_mitm_justification: Source and development builds are delivered over HTTPS from GitLab and r-universe: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr , https://bart-turczynski.r-universe.dev/pagerankr
delivery_unsigned_justification: All distribution downloads are served over HTTPS (GitLab, r-universe): https://bart-turczynski.r-universe.dev/pagerankr
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; SECURITY.md defines the response process and the public tracker is https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No known unfixed critical vulnerabilities exist.
static_analysis_justification: lintr runs as a full-package static analysis check in the GitLab CI gates job: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: R CMD check plus lintr cover common defect classes on every CI pipeline (gates and check jobs): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings must be resolved for the verification gate to pass.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs in the pre-push hook before every push (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.githooks/pre-push) and in the CI gates job on every pipeline, which runs on each push to main (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml).
dynamic_analysis_justification: The testthat suite runs during R CMD check in the CI check job (R 4.6, Linux) and in check-oldrel (R 4.5) on release tags and the scheduled deep check: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: pagerankr contains no compiled source code; it is implemented in R.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: pagerankr's testthat expectations (expect_*) are runtime assertions exercised on every CI run: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Test and check failures block the verification gate.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitLab CI (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml) runs lint, R CMD check and coverage on every push to main and on tags, on self-hosted runners; the same lint and --as-cran check run in the pre-push hook before a change is pushed (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/.githooks/pre-push). Pipelines: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/pipelines
discussion_justification: The GitLab issue tracker provides a public forum for project discussion: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/work_items
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials, secrets, or tokens are committed to the repository: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English (Language: en-US): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/blob/main/README.md
hardening_justification: Hardening mechanisms such as HTTP response headers apply to web applications; pagerankr is an R library.
sites_password_security_justification: pagerankr operates no site that manages user passwords.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained, with current development and routine verification: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/pagerankr/-/commits/main
